summary: A small volunteer-run hackerspace in Duffel, Belgium, where members share a physical workshop and knowledge around electronics, digital technology, and mechanics. It's an open, no-membership-required initiative aimed at anyone locally interested in tinkering rather than a security-focused group; chat happens on Libera IRC.
rules_note: Chat is on Libera IRC (#siscd); no membership fee to participate.

summary: Run by the Stowarzyszenie Hackerspace Pomorze association, this is the Discord server for a physical hackerspace and workshop space in Gdańsk, Poland. Members gather for electronics, making, and general tech projects; the Discord serves mostly as a coordination and chat hub for local members and workshop attendees rather than a global security community.
rules_note: Primarily Polish-language; Discord invite is publicly shared but the group centers on the physical Gdańsk space.

summary: HackerspaceSG is a community-run makerspace in Singapore where volunteers maintain a shared workshop and organize events, from cleanup days to project sessions. It's a general hacker/maker community rather than a dedicated infosec group, with IRC used for day-to-day coordination among members.
rules_note: Chat is on Libera IRC (#hackerspacesg).

summary: Leeds Hackspace is a member-run communal workshop in Leeds, UK, giving people access to tools and equipment (electronics, woodworking, digital fabrication and more) they might not otherwise have. It's an open, welcoming general maker community rather than a security-specific one, with IRC used mainly by existing members for coordination.
rules_note: Chat is on Libera IRC (#leedshackspace); the space itself typically requires a membership fee to access tools.

summary: Shackspace is the Stuttgart hackerspace run by the shack e.V. association, a workshop and clubhouse for nerds and technology enthusiasts covering electronics, software, and general tinkering. It's a general German hacker/maker community, not an infosec-specific group, with chat bridged to Matrix and Libera IRC.
rules_note: Chat is on Matrix, bridged to Libera IRC (#shackspace).

summary: MakeHackVoid, also known as Canberra Makerspace, provides ACT residents with a shared multi-use workshop for building and tinkering projects. It's a general maker community rather than a security-focused one, with a public discussion forum used for coordination among members and prospective visitors.
rules_note: Discussion happens via a public forum requiring registration to post.

summary: A community-run makerspace in Sydney's inner west offering 3D printing, laser cutting, CNC milling, sewing and repair services, with workshops and an after-school program. It is a general maker/craft space rather than a security or hacking group, but its Discord is where members coordinate projects and ask for help with tools.
rules_note: Membership-based physical space; Discord used for coordination, not primarily for security/hacking discussion.

summary: A volunteer-run hackerspace in Saint Petersburg where members hold workshops and lectures spanning soldering, security testing, synthesizers, and software projects. It's a hands-on maker/tech community built on a do-ocracy model rather than a dedicated security shop, welcoming newcomers who message ahead on Telegram before visiting.
rules_note: Message the Telegram chat ahead of visiting in person; new residents should share the space's stated principles.

summary: A Carinthia, Austria-based association promoting cybersecurity awareness and knowledge-sharing, run out of Makerspace Carinthia in Klagenfurt. Members use the Discord to discuss security topics and coordinate regional meetups and events, aimed at both professionals and locals interested in digital security.

The official CCC Würzburg local chapter, a hackerspace of tech enthusiasts meeting weekly at FabLab Würzburg since 2003. Members work on hacker-culture and technology projects together and chat over IRC; it suits people already comfortable in hacker/maker circles more than absolute beginners.
rules_note: Weekly in-person meetup Thursdays 18:30 at FabLab Würzburg; IRC on irc.nerd2nerd.org:6697 (#geeks).

summary: A grassroots skill-exchange hacklab hosted within Zagreb's MaMa club, where tech enthusiasts gather informally and irregularly to share knowledge on various technical topics. Coordination happens mainly over IRC (bridged to Matrix), with no fixed schedule or formal membership process.
rules_note: Best way to reach the community is via IRC (#razmjenavjestina on Libera.Chat); Matrix bridge available; in-person meetups are sporadic.

exclude_reason: Primarily a nonprofit internet service provider (hosting, vServers, domains, peering) rather than an active hacking/security discussion or learning community; no clear public onboarding path for newcomers seeking security content.
summary: A long-running Berlin nonprofit (e.V., founded 1995) that provides internet access, hosting, VPN, and server infrastructure to individuals and NGOs, and operates a small associated hackerspace. It is oriented toward infrastructure and connectivity services rather than security discussion or education for newcomers.
rules_note: Membership application required to join as a provider member; IRC channel #in-berlin on random.ircd.de.

summary: A Zürich makerspace and art collective (SGMK / Bitwäscherei) focused on electronic art, DIY synth building, and soldering workshops rather than security specifically. People drop into weekly open-lab sessions to build projects, learn electronics, and show off work; it suits hands-on hobbyists more than dedicated infosec learners.
run_by: SGMK (Schweizerische Gesellschaft für Mechatronische Kunst), community-run
rules_note: Join via the Matrix room linked from the wiki; weekly open-lab/synth sessions at Bitwäscherei.

summary: This is the Zürich regional chapter of the Swiss Chaos Computer Club, meeting weekly in person at the Bitwäscherei hackspace and online via Jitsi. Members discuss hacking, privacy, and tech-policy issues, and organizers explicitly say the group is not elitist and welcomes newcomers alongside experienced hackers.
run_by: Chaos Computer Club Zürich (CCC-CH regional chapter), community-run
rules_note: Weekly in-person Chaostreff Wednesdays 19:00 at Bitwäscherei; weekly virtual meetup Mondays via Jitsi; join Matrix room for chat.

summary: Rabbithole is the hackerspace run by Chaostreff Osnabrück, a small German civic-tech and hacker collective offering 3D printers, soldering stations, and sensor kits for open experimentation. It's a casual, drop-in workshop space for hackers and tech geeks rather than a dedicated security-training group, also involved in local Code for Osnabrück civic-tech projects.
rules_note: Located on 2nd floor at Uni AStA Osnabrück, not wheelchair accessible; join via Matrix chat link.

summary: Ko-Lab is a nonprofit community workspace in Mechelen, Belgium, run collaboratively by its members as a shared workshop, studio, and social space for science, tech, crafts, and digital art. It's a general makerspace with weekly "Open Friday" drop-in nights rather than a security-focused group.
rules_note: Sign up via the Mattermost invite link on the site; Open Friday nights start 7pm.

summary: This is a small general-purpose makerspace in Milton Keynes, UK, operating as a sub-group of Men in Sheds MK, where members share tools and skills for hands-on projects. It's a general making/DIY community rather than a security or hacking-focused one.
run_by: community-run, affiliated with Men in Sheds MK
rules_note: Join via Slack invite link on the site.

summary: This is the official Discord for MicroPython, the compact Python implementation for microcontrollers created by Damien George and maintained by George Robotics. Members ask troubleshooting questions, share embedded projects, and discuss development of the open-source runtime; it's a general embedded-programming community, not security-focused, though it overlaps with hardware/IoT hacking audiences.
run_by: George Robotics Limited / MicroPython open-source project

summary: A member-run hackerspace in Wrocław, Poland, offering a physical clubhouse and Matrix chat for people working on electronics, software, and other DIY tech projects. It's a general-purpose makerspace with a security-adjacent crowd rather than a dedicated infosec group, suited to locals who want a workshop and community to build things with.
rules_note: Small space (~30 members); chat is bridged/public via Matrix room #public:hswro.org.

summary: MuCCC is the Munich hackerspace and local meeting room for the Chaos Computer Club, hosting regular open evenings, talks, and hands-on tech/hacking projects for around 130 members. It's a general hackerspace culture group (CCC-affiliated) rather than a narrow security-training group, welcoming locals interested in computers, privacy, and hacker ethics.
rules_note: Matrix room bridged to hackint IRC network, common across CCC-affiliated spaces.

summary: Kiberpipa (Cyberpipe) is a long-running community hackerspace/meta-space in Ljubljana, Slovenia, hosting talks and discussions on topics like FOSS, networking, and tech policy alongside general hacking culture. It's community-managed and mostly conducted in Slovenian, fitting locals interested in a broad hacker/maker scene rather than a focused security curriculum.
rules_note: Also reachable via IRC (#kiberpipa on Libera.Chat); site/infra was being rebuilt as of mid-2025.

summary: CCCAC is the regional Chaos Computer Club chapter (Erfakreis Aachen) in Aachen, Germany, running a local hackerspace-style meetup for around 50 members interested in hacking, privacy, and computer culture. It functions as a local CCC affiliate group rather than a structured training program, fitting locals who want in-person hacker community.
rules_note: Matrix room bridged to hackint, the shared IRC network used by many CCC-affiliated spaces.

summary: ChaosStuff is a small hackerspace in Luxembourg City run by the Chaos Computer Club Lëtzebuerg NGO, with an explicit focus on IT security, data integrity, privacy, and hacktivism, including educating newcomers as critical hackers. It suits locals wanting hands-on security/privacy discussion and mentorship in a community clubhouse setting.
rules_note: Chat is a Matrix room bridged via matrix.c3l.lu.

summary: Pixelbar is a community-run hackerspace in Rotterdam with a Discord server used to coordinate weekly open evenings, 3D-printing meetups, board game nights, and hands-on workshops. It's a general maker/hacker clubhouse (not security-focused) that explicitly welcomes newcomers to its recurring events regardless of experience.
rules_note: Open house Wednesday evenings from 7pm; space is up a flight of stairs (accessibility note).

summary: A young Chaostreff (CCC-affiliated hackerspace) in Aalen, Germany, run by a community that grew out of local students and a nearby youth research center. Members meet weekly on Tuesday evenings to work with CNC and laser-cutting tools, electronics, 3D printers, and a self-hosted Kubernetes/FOSS server infrastructure, making it a fit for hobbyists interested in maker projects and self-hosting rather than dedicated offensive/defensive security work.
rules_note: Weekly open meetup Tuesdays 7pm at the Aaccelerator space; join chat via Matrix.

summary: A non-profit, member-run hackerspace based in central Kraków, Poland, offering a shared workshop with 3D printers and electronics tools. People show up for weekly Friday-night open hack sessions and workshops to learn skills, work on personal projects, and meet other local makers; it's a general maker/DIY tech community rather than a cybersecurity-specific group.
rules_note: Drop-in Friday night hacks welcome newcomers; see the wiki's 'first steps' guide before visiting.

summary: A student electronics and hobby club at NTNU in Trondheim, Norway, operating continuously since 1971 as one of the oldest hackerspaces in the world. Members build microcontroller and robotics projects, sew and use a vinyl cutter, and take part in beginner-friendly courses that explicitly require no prior knowledge, making it well suited to NTNU students new to electronics and making rather than a security-focused audience.
rules_note: Open to all NTNU students regardless of major; lifetime membership costs 200 NOK; just show up to join.

summary: A member-run hackerspace (/dev/tal e.V.) in Wuppertal, Germany, centered on a FabLab and a monthly Repair Café where volunteers help fix broken devices. It also runs workshops on topics like CNC machining, oscilloscopes, and LED programming, and explicitly welcomes people with no prior technical experience, making it a general electronics/repair-culture community rather than an infosec-focused one.
rules_note: No prior knowledge needed to attend Repair Café or workshops; join via IRC (Libera.Chat #devtal) or the mailing list.

summary: A small member-run hackspace in Bielefeld, Germany ("A Collective Making Everything"), focused on technology's role in society through hands-on projects like 3D printing, foodhacking (sourdough bread, oat milk), woodworking, and bicycle repair. It runs a weekly open 'Kontextfreier Freitag' meetup and enforces a code of conduct emphasizing inclusivity, but has no particular cybersecurity focus.
rules_note: Weekly open meetup ('Kontextfreier Freitag'); everyone welcome regardless of background; code of conduct enforced.

summary: A community makerspace in Vaasa, Finland, running since 2013 with laser cutting, 3D printing, electronics, and wood/metal workshops plus a dedicated software lab. Weekly no-membership-required open houses on Wednesday evenings let newcomers try the space before joining, and courses range from jewelry-making to arcade builds — a general hobbyist maker community rather than a security-specific one.
rules_note: Open house every Wednesday at 6pm, no membership needed to visit; join chat via Matrix.

summary: CADR is a small volunteer-run hackerspace in Nizhny Novgorod, Russia, offering shared workshop space and equipment for technical projects, hardware tinkering, and self-education. It is a general maker/DIY hackerspace rather than a cybersecurity-focused group, and welcomes newcomers interested in dropping by and learning.
rules_note: Join via Matrix invite link; site and chat are primarily in Russian.

summary: Hackerspace Bremen is a community-run hobby workshop in Bremen, Germany, giving members shared tools and space to build electronics, software, and other DIY projects. It is a general maker/hacker community open to newcomers rather than a dedicated security group, with regular open evenings for anyone curious about tinkering.
rules_note: Join via public Matrix room; site and chat are primarily in German.

summary: Essembly is a makerspace in Esslingen am Neckar, Germany, run by Makerspace Esslingen e.V., offering electronics, 3D printing, networking, and general tinkering space plus monthly open workshops. It is a general tech/maker community, not security-specific, and explicitly welcomes people to just drop in and try things out.
rules_note: Join via public Matrix room; site is primarily in German.

summary: Hackeskur is a newly founded (2025) hackerspace in Hvidovre near Copenhagen, Denmark, connected to the Labitat hacker community. It appears to be a general-purpose hacker/maker meetup space; the group's IRC channel is the main way to reach them since the space is still young.
rules_note: Join via IRC on irc.labitat.dk, channel #hackeskur; no official website found, wiki page was accessible only via hackerspaces.org.
red_flags: Very new group (founded Feb 2025) with minimal online presence; details could not be independently verified beyond the hackerspaces.org wiki listing.

summary: Chaostreff Bern is a registered association and hackerspace in Bern, Switzerland, hosting thematic tech evenings, talks (e.g. home automation), keysigning parties, and involvement in Swiss digital-rights campaigns against surveillance legislation. It suits people interested in general tech tinkering and digital privacy/independence, with regular open house days for newcomers.
rules_note: Join via public Matrix room; site primarily in German with some English.

summary: Chaos Computer Club Basel is a Swiss hackerspace near Basel offering weekly open evenings, technical workshops (e.g. Linux installation), talks on topics like DNSSEC and retro computing, and tours of infrastructure sites. It is a general hacker/tech community rather than a security-specialist group, welcoming visitors to its open Tuesday nights.
rules_note: Join via public Matrix room; open house every Tuesday from 7:30 PM; site primarily in German.

summary: A member-run makerspace in Edmonton offering shared woodworking, electronics, metalworking, and pottery studios with 24/7 access for members. It's general maker/hobbyist space rather than security-focused, but overlaps with hardware tinkering and DIY electronics that adjacent hackers may enjoy.
rules_note: Paid membership required for facility access; Matrix chat is public to join.

summary: A long-running hackerspace in Bochum, Germany, part of the German Chaos hacker scene, where members tinker with electronics, computing, and DIY projects. It's a general hacker/maker collective rather than a dedicated infosec group, appealing to locally-based tech tinkerers of varied skill levels.
rules_note: Public wiki and Matrix room; in-person meetups happen at the space.

summary: The Bonn "Chaostreff" hackspace, meeting weekly for an open evening plus monthly Raspberry Pi workshops, lockpicking, 3D printing, and Linux installs. It explicitly welcomes newcomers with no prior knowledge, making it a friendly entry point for beginners interested in hands-on tech and light security topics like lockpicking.
rules_note: No prior knowledge needed; open Tuesday evenings at Bornheimer Straße 25.

summary: A hackerspace in Yerevan founded by an international group of tech enthusiasts, offering 3D printers, laser cutters, and soldering stations, with workshops ranging from 3D printing to neural networks. It's a general maker/tech community rather than security-specific, run mostly in Russian with semi-open Friday meetups.
rules_note: Contact via Telegram (@HackerEmbassyBot or @hacker_embassy); semi-open Friday meetings at 8 PM.

summary: A hackerspace in Arnhem, Netherlands, with electronics labs, a computer museum, woodshop, and library, open to the public on Tuesday and Friday evenings. Members work on soldering, programming, laser cutting, and other DIY projects; it's a general tinkerer/maker community with only incidental security angle.
rules_note: Open house Tuesday and Friday evenings from 19:00; also reachable via IRC (#hack42 on OFTC).

summary: Hackspace Rostock is a weekly-meeting community workshop for tech enthusiasts to tinker with hardware and software, share knowledge, and run projects like Linux workshops and notebook recycling. It's a general hacker/maker space open to anyone curious about technology, not security-specific.
rules_note: Open every Wednesday from 19:00 at Friedhofsweg 44a; Matrix chat and membership form available.

summary: This is the chat for Nobreakspace, a hackerspace run by the Chaotikum e.V. association in Lübeck, Germany. Members hold weekly open evenings and workshops on Linux, password managers, privacy tools, soldering and 3D printing, and organize a small annual conference called Nights of Open Knowledge; it's a general tech/maker community with a digital-rights bent rather than a dedicated security research group.
rules_note: Open Space/Chaostreff meetups happen regularly at the physical space; join via Matrix room linked from the site.

summary: This Discord serves York Hackspace, a member-run makerspace in York, UK, founded in 2011 as part of the UK Hackspace Foundation. People meet at weekly open evenings to work on electronics, woodworking, 3D printing and other DIY projects, and paying members get 24/7 access to the physical space's tools; it's a general maker/DIY community rather than an information-security focused one.
rules_note: Open evenings most Wednesdays for members and visitors; join the mailing list and Discord to get started, paid membership needed for space access.

summary: Chaostreff Backnang is a small, community-run hacker/maker meetup in Backnang, Germany, part of the wider German Chaostreff network loosely affiliated with the Chaos Computer Club scene. They gather on the third Sunday of each month in a shared community space to swap knowledge and work on projects together, covering general tech and hacking topics rather than one narrow specialty.
rules_note: Meets in person monthly (3rd Sunday) at dasWohnzimmer, Willy-Brandt-Platz 2; join chat via Matrix.

summary: Fablab Chemnitz, run by the German association Stadtfabrikanten e.V., is a community fab lab/makerspace where members build shared knowledge and collaborate on hardware, 3D-printing, electronics and software projects. It's a general maker and open-hardware community rather than a security-focused one, open to locals wanting hands-on project space.
rules_note: Join chat via Matrix; open lab hours at the physical space.

summary: Foulab is a member-run, member-funded hackerspace in Montreal founded in 2008, one of the first hackerspaces in Canada. Members get a shared, well-equipped workshop to explore technology, electronics and software hands-on and share knowledge; it's a general hacker/maker community rather than a dedicated infosec group, coordinated over IRC (#foulab on Libera Chat).
rules_note: Chat is #foulab on Libera Chat (irc.libera.chat); no signup needed to join the IRC channel.

summary: Entropia e.V. is the official Karlsruhe local chapter (Erfa-Kreis) of the German Chaos Computer Club, founded in 1999 out of the local Chaostreff. Members hold weekly open meetings on Sunday evenings covering hacking, privacy, reverse engineering and security/tech-policy topics, and the group organizes the Gulaschprogrammiernacht, one of the CCC's largest annual events after the Chaos Communication Congress.
rules_note: Open weekly meetings Sundays 19:30 at Gewerbehof, Steinstr. 23; join chat via Matrix.

summary: Flipdot is a hackerspace in Kassel, Germany, run as a local CCC group, offering a clubroom where members and visitors tinker on electronics, software, and general hacker-culture projects. It holds regular public open hours and workshops, and coordinates over Matrix, its wiki, and Mastodon.
rules_note: Open nearly every day with a public open evening weekly; the Matrix room is linked from the website.

summary: Attraktor is a large makerspace and hackerspace in Hamburg, Germany, offering metal- and woodworking, electronics, CNC, 3D printing, and software workshops for tinkerers and hobbyists. It has historically hosted Chaos Computer Club Hamburg activities alongside its own member-run projects, and coordinates via a Matrix room.
rules_note: Space is member-run; check current opening hours on the website before visiting.
red_flags: A former board member's ties to far-right activity led CCC to end its office arrangement with the space in 2019; the space itself continues operating independently.

summary: Codinglab is a small computer club and hackerspace in Minusio, near Locarno in Switzerland, where members hold biweekly labs to build skills on varied technical topics. It suits local hobbyists looking for an in-person, hands-on tech community rather than an online-first one.
rules_note: IRC channel requires a password (per invite_url); ask via the website to get access, and note the group is quite small (~10 members).

summary: Coredump is a combined hacker- and makerspace in Rapperswil-Jona, Switzerland, with an electronics workshop (soldering stations, SMD oven, PCB etching) and woodworking tools for members' personal projects. It runs a weekly open hacknight where guests are welcome, making it an easy first visit for newcomers in the area.
rules_note: Guests are welcome at the weekly Monday hacknight; join chat via the IRC/Libera channel or the website for details.

summary: Kaouenn-noz is a biohackerspace and DIY-science collective based in Rennes, France, focused on bioart, biohacking, biodesign, and hands-on life-science and environmental projects (such as a water-quality initiative called Hack2Eaux). It suits people interested in citizen science and biology-adjacent hacking more than traditional infosec, and coordinates through a shared Matrix biohacking room.
rules_note: Matrix room (#diybio-biohacking:matrix.org) is a general DIY-bio room shared across groups, not exclusive to this space.

summary: C3RE is a Chaostreff (informal CCC-affiliated meetup group) in the Recklinghausen district of Germany, meeting weekly in a clubhouse called the Hackerhütte on the grounds of a former coal mine. Members discuss projects, tech, and net-politics topics and help each other with tools and tips in a casual, low-pressure setting.
rules_note: Meets every Wednesday at the Hackerhütte; Matrix room linked from the website.

summary: This is the Discord for L.A.B (Laboratoire d'Aix-périmentation et de Bidouille), a member-run fablab and hackerspace in Aix-en-Provence, France, offering 3D printing, laser cutting, CNC milling and electronics. Members use it to coordinate weekly workshop sessions, gaming nights, and maker/STEAM projects; it's general maker culture with some electronics/hardware hacking rather than a dedicated security focus, and suits locals wanting hands-on hardware help.
rules_note: Primarily a French-language local fablab community; open sessions Tuesdays/Wednesdays evenings.

summary: Metalab is Vienna's oldest community-run hackspace, offering laser cutters, 3D printers, CNC mills and electronics labs for members and visitors interested in art, technology, society and science. Interest groups cover networking, ham radio, electronics and robotics; it's a general maker/hacker community rather than security-specific, welcoming newcomers to open days and evening drop-ins.
rules_note: Space generally open after 6pm daily; open days second Thursday and fourth Friday of the month; Matrix room is a low-traffic lobby channel.

summary: This is the Discord run by CCC Darmstadt (the local Chaos Computer Club chapter, also called Chaos Darmstadt), used to coordinate meetups, hacking/hardware sessions and CTF-adjacent activity since in-person organizing capacity has been limited. It's a small, low-traffic community oriented around German hacker/CCC culture rather than a dedicated beginner-training space.
run_by: CCC Darmstadt (Chaos Computer Club local chapter)
rules_note: Small server (~40 members); regular organized in-person meetings have been paused, Discord is the fallback coordination channel.

summary: This is the Matrix lobby for CCC Wiesbaden (CCCWI), a local Chaos Computer Club-affiliated hackspace despite the listing name 'CCC Mainz'; the group explicitly says newcomers are welcome whether or not they have a technical background. People use it to chat and coordinate weekly Tuesday-evening meetups at the space, covering general hacking, tech and privacy topics.
rules_note: Actual location is Wiesbaden, not Mainz, despite the entry's given name; open evening Tuesdays from 7pm.

summary: Warszawski Hackerspace is a community-run creative/maker space in Warsaw with a heavy workshop (CNC, laser, lathe, welding) and an electronics lab, open to anyone with ideas or a need for tools. It hosts weekly open Thursday-evening meetings and workshops on machine building and radio technology; people join via IRC, Matrix or email, and can become members after visiting a few times.
rules_note: Weekly open house Thursdays 6pm; several visits typically expected before joining as a full member.

summary: Breizh-Entropy is a small informal hackerspace collective in Rennes, France, that grew out of the Breizh Entropy Congress (BEC) hacker conference. It runs a weekly Wednesday-evening open session at its local space and uses IRC on Libera.Chat as its main chat/coordination channel for members and visitors interested in hacking, electronics and free/open-source culture.
rules_note: Join #breizh-entropy on irc.libera.chat (TLS port 6697) to reach the group and request space access; open Wednesdays 18:30-21:00.
